items.difficulty_reason: For a ringed space Y, a sheaf of ideals I, the quotient O_X = O_Y/I and N = SheafHom_{O_Y}(I/I^2, O_X), the lemma asserts a canonical isomorphism c : N -> SheafExt^1_{O_Y}(O_X, O_X) (statement lines 3619-3658). The proof starts from the short exact sequence 0 -> I/I^2 -> O_Y/I^2 -> O_X -> 0 of equation labelled equation-second-order-thickening, and for an open U and a section s in N(U) pushes this sequence out along s to obtain an extension E_s of O_X|_U by itself, which defines the section c(s) of SheafExt^1 via Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-section-RHom-over-U and Derived Categories, Lemma labelled derived-lemma-ext-1 (proof lines 3660-3674). For the converse, an extension 0 -> O_X -> E -> O_X -> 0 on U admits an open covering with sections e_i lifting 1, and each e_i defines a map O_Y|_{U_i} -> E|_{U_i} whose kernel contains I^2, so the extension comes from a pushout as above; this proves that c is surjective (proof lines 3676-3688). The proof then states that the proof of injectivity is omitted (proof lines 3688-3689). Turning an extension into a map out of the conormal sheaf by pushout, and reversing the construction via local lifts of the unit section, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2; the omitted injectivity is recorded verbatim in the notes.
